title: United States Loses Measles-Free Status as Cases Reach Record Highs
subtitle: Public health officials confirm the country no longer meets the criteria for measles elimination after a sharp rise in infections and deaths.

summary.en: The United States has officially lost its measles-free status following a widespread outbreak. Health officials report nearly 5,500 cases and 10 deaths across the country. Experts point to declining vaccination rates since the COVID-19 pandemic as the primary cause. New research also highlights the dangerous rise of measles in pregnant women and infants. Public health leaders are now calling for better access to vaccines to regain control of the disease.
summary.zh: 美國在經歷大規模疫情後，已正式失去「麻疹消除國」的地位。衛生官員通報全國累計近五千五百例確診與十起死亡案例。專家指出，自新冠肺炎疫情以來疫苗接種率下降是主要原因。最新研究亦凸顯了孕婦與嬰兒感染麻疹的危險性增加。公共衛生領袖目前正呼籲改善疫苗取得管道，以重新控制疫情。

paragraphs.en: The United States has officially lost its measles-free status, a major public health setback that confirms the country is no longer free from the continuous spread of the disease. A panel of experts from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) reviewed national data and concluded that the U.S. no longer meets the requirements for elimination. This status, which the U.S. held since 2000, meant that the same strain of the virus had not been spreading for at least 12 months. That is no longer the case, as outbreaks have continued to flare across the country for more than a year.
paragraphs.zh: 美國已正式失去「麻疹消除國」的地位，這是一項重大的公共衛生挫敗，證實該國已無法再阻斷此疾病的持續傳播。泛美衛生組織（Pan American Health Organization, PAHO）的一個專家小組審查了全國數據後得出結論，認為美國已不再符合消除麻疹的條件。美國自二〇〇〇年以來一直保持此地位，意即同一病毒株在境內已至少十二個月未出現持續傳播。然而情況已非如此，因為疫情在過去一年多以來持續在全國各地爆發。

paragraphs.en: According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the national tally of confirmed cases has reached nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions. This is more than double the total number of cases reported in 2025. Tragically, the outbreak has resulted in 10 deaths, including at least four infants. Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin recently announced two additional deaths, marking the first time in decades that these states have seen such losses. Pennsylvania alone has reported over 1,500 cases, while Wisconsin has recorded nearly 650.
paragraphs.zh: 根據疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）的數據，全國累計確診病例已達近五千五百例，遍及四十七個州與司法管轄區。這數字是二〇二五年通報病例總數的兩倍以上。令人遺憾的是，這波疫情已造成十人死亡，其中包括至少四名嬰兒。賓夕法尼亞州與威斯康辛州的衛生官員近期宣布了兩起新增死亡案例，這是這兩個州數十年來首次出現此類死亡事件。僅賓夕法尼亞州就通報了超過一千五百例病例，而威斯康辛州則記錄了近六百五十例。

paragraphs.en: Medical experts note that this shift is largely due to declining vaccination rates. The percentage of children entering kindergarten with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine has dropped since the COVID-19 pandemic. Currently, only 10 states reach the target of 95% vaccination coverage. While many families want to vaccinate their children, some report difficulty accessing care, confusion about insurance, or problems with vaccine recommendations. Despite these barriers, public opinion remains largely supportive of vaccines, with a strong majority of American adults believing that the benefits of the MMR vaccine outweigh the risks.
paragraphs.zh: 醫學專家指出，這種轉變主要歸因於疫苗接種率的下降。自新冠肺炎疫情以來，入學幼兒接種麻疹、腮腺炎與德國麻疹（MMR）混合疫苗的比率已有所下滑。目前僅有十個州達到百分之九十五的接種覆蓋率目標。儘管許多家庭希望為孩子接種疫苗，但部分民眾反映在取得醫療服務上遇到困難、對保險規定感到困惑，或是對疫苗建議存有疑慮。儘管存在這些障礙，大眾對疫苗的支持度依然很高，絕大多數美國成年人認為接種 MMR 疫苗的益處大於風險。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the general population, the current outbreak is causing new and serious health concerns. Researchers from the CDC recently highlighted a rise in congenital measles—cases where the virus is passed from a mother to her baby during pregnancy. Between early 2025 and September 2026, there were 112 confirmed cases of measles in pregnant women. Nearly all of these women had not received the MMR vaccine or had an unknown vaccination history. Michael Osterholm, who directs the University of Minnesota's Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy, described this as a brand-new phenomenon. He explained that because measles was kept under control for so long, many women of childbearing age have never been exposed to the virus, leaving them highly susceptible to infection.
paragraphs.zh: 除了普通民眾之外，目前的疫情正引發新的嚴重健康隱憂。CDC 的研究人員近期強調了先天性麻疹病例的增加，即病毒在懷孕期間由母親傳染給胎兒的情況。在二〇二五年初至二〇二六年九月期間，共確認了一百一十二例孕婦感染麻疹的病例。這些女性幾乎都沒有接種過 MMR 疫苗，或是疫苗接種史不明。明尼蘇達大學傳染病研究與政策中心主任奧斯特霍姆（Michael Osterholm）將此描述為一種全新的現象。他解釋說，由於麻疹長期以來受到控制，許多育齡女性從未接觸過該病毒，導致她們對感染極為脆弱。

paragraphs.en: Measles in pregnancy is linked to severe outcomes, including a higher risk of hospitalization, pneumonia, and death for the mother. Infants born to infected mothers are more likely to be born early, and some infants have already developed serious symptoms, including fever, rash, and in at least one case, meningoencephalitis—a dangerous swelling of the brain. Adam Ratner, a member of the American Academy of Pediatrics' infectious diseases committee, noted that when measles is properly controlled, these congenital cases do not happen.
paragraphs.zh: 懷孕期間感染麻疹與嚴重的後果有關，包括母親住院、罹患肺炎及死亡的風險增加。感染孕婦所生的嬰兒更有可能早產，且部分嬰兒已出現嚴重症狀，包括發燒、出疹，以及至少一例腦膜腦炎——一種危險的腦部腫脹。美國兒科學會傳染病委員會成員拉特納（Adam Ratner）指出，當麻疹受到妥善控制時，這些先天性病例是不會發生的。

paragraphs.en: Despite the loss of elimination status, health officials believe the situation can be reversed. CDC director Erica Schwartz stated that the agency plans to focus on education and improving access to vaccines. Experts point to successful public health campaigns in other parts of the world as evidence that population-level immunity can be restored. The path forward requires making it easier and more affordable for families to get vaccinated, ensuring that healthcare systems are prepared to manage the current surge, and addressing the logistical barriers that prevent many people from receiving care.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管失去了消除地位，衛生官員認為情況仍可扭轉。CDC 主任施瓦茨（Erica Schwartz）表示，該機構計畫將重點放在衛教宣導與改善疫苗取得管道上。專家以世界其他地區成功的公共衛生運動為例，證明群體免疫是可以恢復的。未來的路徑需要讓家庭能更輕鬆且負擔得起地接種疫苗，確保醫療系統準備好應對當前的疫情激增，並解決阻礙許多民眾獲得照護的物流障礙。

paragraphs.en: While the loss of status is a significant warning, experts emphasize that the trend is not permanent. By increasing vaccination rates and strengthening public health outreach, the U.S. aims to stop the spread and eventually regain its measles-free standing. For now, clinicians and hospitals remain on high alert as they work to manage the highest number of measles cases seen in the country in three decades.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然失去地位是一個重大的警訊，但專家強調這種趨勢並非永久性的。透過提高疫苗接種率並加強公共衛生宣導，美國目標在於遏止傳播並最終恢復其麻疹消除國的地位。目前，臨床醫師與醫院仍保持高度警戒，致力於應對該國三十年來最嚴重的麻疹疫情。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To suddenly start or become much worse.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （疾病、暴力或問題）突然爆發、加劇。
keyTerms.noteZh: 通常指火焰燃燒，這裡用來形容疾病傳播。文中：as outbreaks have continued to flare across the country for more than a year.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be greater or more significant than something else.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由 out-（超過）與 weigh（重量）組成，指價值或重要性超過某物。文中：with a strong majority of American adults believing that the benefits of the MMR vaccine outweigh the risks.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Easily influenced or harmed by something, such as a disease.
keyTerms.noteZh: 在醫學語境中常指身體缺乏抵抗力。文中：leaving them highly susceptible to infection.
原意指海浪湧起，這裡形容病例數量的快速上升。文中：ensuring that healthcare systems are prepared to manage the current surge, and addressing the logistical barriers that prevent many people from receiving care.

quiz.question: According to the article, what specific condition must be met for the U.S. to be considered 'measles-free'?

options.A: A vaccination rate of at least 95% in all 50 states.
options.B: The absence of continuous transmission of the same virus strain for 12 months.
options.C: A total national tally of fewer than 100 confirmed cases per year.
options.D: The complete eradication of the virus from all pregnant women.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，美國曾保持「無麻疹」狀態，其定義為同一種病毒株在至少 12 個月內沒有持續傳播。選項 A 是目前疫苗接種的目標，但並非定義「無麻疹」狀態的官方標準。選項 C 是錯誤推論，文章並未設定具體的病例數字作為標準。選項 D 雖然提到孕婦案例，但這與國家層級的「無麻疹」狀態定義無關。

quiz.question: Why does Michael Osterholm describe the rise in congenital measles as a 'brand-new phenomenon'?

options.A: Because doctors have only recently developed the technology to test for measles during pregnancy.
options.B: Because the virus has mutated into a new, more dangerous form that specifically targets infants.
options.C: Because previous decades of effective control meant women of childbearing age lacked natural immunity.
options.D: Because the virus was previously thought to be unable to cross the placenta to reach the fetus.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，由於麻疹長期受到控制，許多育齡女性從未接觸過病毒，導致她們缺乏免疫力，這才使得先天性麻疹成為新興問題。選項 A 與文章內容無關，文中並未提及檢測技術的突破。選項 B 是錯誤推論，文章並未提及病毒突變。選項 D 錯誤，文中並未聲稱病毒先前被認為無法穿過胎盤，而是強調了缺乏免疫力導致的易感性。

quiz.question: In the first paragraph, what does the word 'flare' mean as used in the context of the measles outbreak?

options.A: To suddenly become intense or active.
options.B: To burn with a bright, steady light.
options.C: To widen at the bottom of a garment.
options.D: To show anger or strong emotion.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在第一段中，「outbreaks have continued to flare」意指疫情突然爆發或活躍起來。選項 B 是指火焰燃燒，雖然與「flare」的原意相關，但在這裡是用於描述疾病傳播的隱喻。選項 C 是指衣服下擺變寬，與語境完全不符。選項 D 是指情緒激動，雖然「flare up」可用於情緒，但在描述疾病時，它指的是疫情的加劇而非情緒反應。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the current measles situation in the U.S.?

options.A: The U.S. healthcare system is permanently damaged and cannot recover from the measles outbreak.
options.B: The rise in cases is primarily due to a lack of public support for the MMR vaccine.
options.C: The loss of measles-free status is a serious setback, but experts believe it can be reversed through better access and education.
options.D: Congenital measles is the only reason the U.S. lost its status as a measles-free nation.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章總結了美國失去無麻疹狀態的事實，並在最後兩段強調了衛生官員對未來復甦的信心，透過教育與改善疫苗可及性來解決問題。選項 A 錯誤，文章明確指出趨勢並非永久。選項 B 與文章內容矛盾，文中提到公眾對疫苗的支持度依然很高。選項 D 錯誤，先天性麻疹只是疫情的嚴重影響之一，並非導致失去地位的唯一原因。
